headline: Protests erupt as Bangladesh signs 15-year deal with DP World to operate NCT
summary: Port protection committees and labor organizations announce a mass hunger strike for Monday following the concession agreement for the New Mooreing Container Terminal.
details: Bangladesh has signed a 15-year concession agreement with Dubai-based DP World to operate the New Mooreing Container Terminal (NCT) at Chattogram port.
The deal was signed on Thursday afternoon at the Invest Bangladesh Auditorium, amidst protests from various leftist groups and labor organizations.
The Port Protection Committee, along with several worker organizations, announced a mass hunger strike for Monday, October 12, following a rally in front of the port.
Protesters claim that handing over the NCT to a foreign operator threatens the port's security and national sovereignty.
Demonstrators described the agreement as 'suicidal' and demanded a reconsideration of the decision, alleging that terms were kept secret and public opinion was ignored.
Clashes occurred in front of the Invest Bangladesh Auditorium, where police intervened to disperse protesters and used batons to maintain order.
caption:
A 15-year deal to operate the NCT has sparked mass protests and a planned hunger strike in Chattogram.

Bangladesh has signed a 15-year concession agreement with Dubai-based DP World to operate the New Mooreing Container Terminal (NCT) at Chattogram port.

The deal was signed on Thursday afternoon at the Invest Bangladesh Auditorium, amidst protests from various leftist groups and labor organizations.

The Port Protection Committee, along with several worker organizations, announced a mass hunger strike for Monday, October 12, following a rally in front of the port.

Protesters claim that handing over the NCT to a foreign operator threatens the port's security and national sovereignty.

Demonstrators described the agreement as 'suicidal' and demanded a reconsideration of the decision, alleging that terms were kept secret and public opinion was ignored.

Clashes occurred in front of the Invest Bangladesh Auditorium, where police intervened to disperse protesters and used batons to maintain order.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Jamuna TV, Prothom Alo, bdnews24.com

headline: Tk 17.4m gold seized: Customs recover 1.29kg of 'gold eggs' from passenger at Dhaka airport
summary: Three oval-shaped pieces of 24-carat gold paste, concealed in the passenger's rectum, were uncovered by customs officers at Shahjalal International Airport.
details: Customs officers at Shahjalal International Airport seized 1.29kg of 24-carat gold paste from a passenger arriving from Sharjah, UAE.
The National Board of Revenue (NBR) reported that a preventive team began surveillance after receiving a tip-off regarding Air Arabia flight G9 518.
Passenger Arman Uddin Siddique was stopped for a search after completing immigration and reaching baggage belt-2.
The search revealed three oval-shaped pieces of gold paste, dubbed 'gold eggs', wrapped in white cellotape and concealed in his rectum.
Each 'egg' weighed 430g, totaling 1.29kg. The NBR stated that refining the paste could yield approximately 1,000g of pure gold.
The seized gold is estimated to be worth Tk 17.4 million.
Dhaka Customs House is now preparing to file a criminal case against the passenger.
caption:
1.29kg of gold hidden in the rectum! Customs officers at Dhaka airport have seized 'gold eggs' worth Tk 17.4 million.

Customs officers at Shahjalal International Airport seized 1.29kg of 24-carat gold paste from a passenger arriving from Sharjah, UAE.

The National Board of Revenue (NBR) reported that a preventive team began surveillance after receiving a tip-off regarding Air Arabia flight G9 518.

Passenger Arman Uddin Siddique was stopped for a search after completing immigration and reaching baggage belt-2.

The search revealed three oval-shaped pieces of gold paste, dubbed 'gold eggs', wrapped in white cellotape and concealed in his rectum.

Each 'egg' weighed 430g, totaling 1.29kg. The NBR stated that refining the paste could yield approximately 1,000g of pure gold.

The seized gold is estimated to be worth Tk 17.4 million.

Dhaka Customs House is now preparing to file a criminal case against the passenger.
